Video Title: Guadeloupe Ash Wednesday Street Party & The Burning of King Vaval
Description:
Experiencing Mercredi des Cendres (Ash Wednesday) in Guadeloupe is something you will never forget. Marking the official end of the Guadeloupe Carnival season, thousands of revelers take over the streets of Pointe-à-Pitre and Basse-Terre wearing traditional black and white attire.

In this video, we jump right into the heart of the final "vidé" street party, surrounded by the hypnotic rhythms of traditional drums, before witnessing the main event: the ritual burning of Sa Majesté Vaval (the Carnival King). Vaval is built every year to represent a major news event or social theme, and his cremation acts as a cathartic rebirth for the island before Lent begins.
